Born in England in September 1621, son of Reverend John Wilson, first minister of Boston,
with whom he came over; in Harvard's first graduating class, 1642.
Assistant to Richard Mather at Dorchester from 1649, then from December 1651 minister,
physician and schoolmaster of Medfield for nearly forty years.
In King Philip's War his house served as a hospital for wounded soldiers.
Died at Medfield on the Sabbath, 23 August 1691.
Daughter of Reverend Thomas Hooker, founder of Hartford, and wife of Reverend John Wilson of Medfield,
whose 1691 will calls her "the faithful companion of my youth and old age" and makes her sole executrix.
Mother of Sarah (Mrs. Paul Batt, then Mrs. Josiah Torrey) , Elizabeth (Mrs. Thomas Weld) and Susanna (Mrs. Grindall Rawson)
